`GET /` returns a usage hint immediately. The router sends single-segment paths such as `GET /1` to a handler
that waits for 250 ms, reads `id` with `routeMatch($request)?->param('id')` and returns `1`.
The router decodes the parameter, so `GET /a%20b` returns `a b`.

## Run

Use 64-bit PHP 8.6 with `Io\Poll\Context` and ext-pcntl on Unix. Once the split is on Packagist, install
the development version with Composer.

```sh
composer create-project thesis/demo demo dev-main
cd demo
php run.php
```

From the monorepo root, run `make install`, then start the server in Docker.

```sh
docker compose run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 php php packages/demo/run.php 0.0.0.0:8080
```

In another terminal, send the same eight requests sequentially and then concurrently.

```sh
time curl -fsS 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/[1-8]'
time curl -fsS --parallel --parallel-immediate 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/[1-8]'
```

On an idle machine, expect about two seconds for the first command and about 250 ms for the second.
The console shows the path and duration of each finished request. Press Ctrl+C to stop the server and drain its logs.

The server and logger are wired in [run.php](run.php).
